$Comment: Authoritative DEFAULT mob-scaling settings, decoded via MobScalingSettingsAsset.CODEC (PascalCase keys, nested groups). Read synchronously at plugin setup() so the registration gate can see Enabled. Owners override any key in mods/MmoMobScaling/mob-scaling.json (the same PascalCase shape, partial allowed - a nested group may be partially filled), and a preset file beside this one overlays only the keys it lists. HOW A SPOT'S DIFFICULTY IS FOUND: its zone or biome floor (the Difficulty/*.json mappings, rising outward from Zone1 at 1 to Zone4_Tier5 at 28) plus the DistanceEscalation bonus, plus the nearby group's power delta outside the protected ring, clamped to MinCap..MaxCap. A rarity or variant then multiplies that number by its own DifficultyMultiplier before the curve is read, so a Legendary at 30 is folded like a plain mob at 72; that product is deliberately not clamped to MaxCap, which is why a Legendary and a Boss still differ at the top of the scale. DistanceEscalation.BlocksPerPoint is 87 so the top of the scale is actually reachable: from the 5000-block start, the highest shipped zone floor of 28 needs 172 more points to reach MaxCap 200, and 172 times 87 is 14,964 blocks, so the cap sits about 19,964 blocks from spawn (with a lower floor the ramp runs to MaxBonus 199 instead). StartDistanceBlocks is 5000 to match the protected ring, so outside that ring player scaling and the distance ramp begin together. Stand where you want the ramp to start and read the distance off /mobscaling inspect rather than guessing; the reading comes from the spawning chunk's centre, so it steps 32 blocks at a time. HOW THE CURVE IS TUNED: the curve is set so a plain mob at difficulty N is an even fight for a player whose power is N, all the way up. Over a full progression a character comes to absorb about 58 times the damage it could at the start but deals only about 11 times the damage per second, so an even mob at the top must hit about 58 times harder while taking only about 11 times as long to kill. That is why the damage axis climbs so much further than the toughness axis: a mob that is hard only because it is a sponge is the wrong kind of hard. The toughness axis is a straight line: EffectiveHpPerPoint 0.0525 reaches 11.45 times at difficulty 200. The damage axis is a curve, 1 + OutDamageScale times (difficulty - 1) to the power OutDamageShape. A shape of 1.0 is a straight line and the scale is then a plain per-point slope; a shape above 1.0 bends the curve upward, so for the same top value the early difficulties hit gently and the late ones hit hard, and a shape below 1.0 does the reverse. The 1.4 here follows how a character actually toughens up: slowly at first, then fast through the middle levels as the defence picks and the armour arrive, so a straight line that is right at the top would hit a low-level character nearly twice as hard as an even fight should. With scale 0.0342 a plain mob hits about 5 times its base at difficulty 32, about 22 times at 100 and about 58 times at 200. VisibleHpShare 0.85 puts most of the toughness on the health bar, where it can be read, and leaves the rest as silent damage reduction; the two always multiply back to the same time to kill, so this knob changes how a fight looks, not how long it lasts. THE TWO RAILS, MaxEffectiveHpMult and MaxOutDamageMult, each sit just past what a Boss reads at the top of the scale. A Boss reads the curve at three times the spot's difficulty, so at MaxCap 200 it reads at 600: about 32 times an unscaled mob's toughness and about 266 times its hit, under the rails of 34.4 and 270. A rail at the plain mob's own top value is what flattens the rarity ladder: every tier reaches it and a Legendary stops differing from a Boss. Set past the boss, the rails are anti-runaway safety and nothing else; lower them and the ladder collapses from the top down. The damage rail sits much further above the plain top (58) than the toughness rail sits above its own (11.45) because the damage curve bends upward: three times the difficulty is about 4.6 times the hit but only about 2.8 times the toughness. Difficulty.MaxCap may sit ABOVE the MMO's player-power ceiling, and that is the only way for mobs to out-scale a fully geared group, since player power cannot push past its own maximum; MaxOutDamageMult is then what limits how hard those mobs hit. Clamps are the safety rails that are not the curve's shape, applied per axis after an affix's fold deltas: MaxLootMult 4.0 leaves room for a boss carrying an overlay (3.0 times 1.3 loot passes) to pay out in full.

Origin.$Comment: Where the distance is measured from. Left empty, as here, it is the world's own spawn point, so nothing needs setting on a world with one spawn point. Set X and Z, in blocks (a minus sign is fine, and whole blocks are all the precision the ramp has, since it reads the centre of the chunk a mob spawns in), to measure from somewhere else: a world whose spawn provider holds several spawn points reads one of them and not necessarily the first, and a home city away from where players first appear is better measured from the city. An axis you leave out keeps following the spawn point on its own. This moves the escalation ramp only; the protected ring around spawn under OpenWorld.PlayerScalingStartRingBlocks stays centred on the spawn point. /mobscaling inspect reports the distance from spawn where you stand, which is the number to compare against StartDistanceBlocks.
